vsm2.17:19.2:
This total conditionally, acting interdependently,
Arouses states together equally;
So this too is a reason here wherefore the Greatest Sage,
the Seer, Gave to this term its form thus succinctly.
vsm2.17:20.1:
20. Among the conditions described under the headings of ignorance, etc., the respective conditions
that make the conditionally-arisen states beginning with formations arise
vsm2.17:20.2: are incapable of making them arise when not mutually dependent and when deficient.
vsm2.17:20.3:
Therefore this conditionality by depending (paṭicca—ger.) makes states arise (uppādeti)
equally and together (samaṃ saha ca), not piecemeal and successively
vsm2.17:20.4:
—so it has been termed here thus by the Sage who is skilled in phraseology that conforms to its meaning:
it has been accurately termed “dependent origination” (paṭicca samuppāda), is the meaning.
vsm2.17:21.1:
21. And while so termed:

The first component will deny the false view of eternity
And so on, and the second will prevent
The nihilistic type of view and others like it, while the two
Together show the true way that is meant.
vsm2.17:21.2: The first: the word “dependent” (paṭicca) indicates the combination of the conditions,
vsm2.17:21.3: since states in the process of occurring exist in dependence on the combining of their conditions;
vsm2.17:21.4:
and it shows that they are not eternal, etc., thus denying the various doctrines of eternalism,
no-cause, fictitious-cause, and power-wielder.
vsm2.17:21.5: What purpose indeed would the combining of conditions serve, if things were eternal, or if they occurred without cause, and so on?
vsm2.17:23.1: 23. The second: the word “origination” (samuppāda) indicates the arising of the states,
vsm2.17:23.2: since these occur when their conditions combine,
vsm2.17:23.3:
and it shows how to prevent annihilationism, etc., thus preventing the various doctrines of annihilation of a soul,
nihilism, “there is no use in giving,” etc., and moral-inefficacy-of-action, “there is no other world,” etc.;
vsm2.17:23.4: for when states are seen to arise again and again, each conditioned by its predecessor,
vsm2.17:23.5: how can the doctrines of annihilationism, nihilism, and moral-inefficacy-of-action be maintained?
vsm2.17:24.1:
24. The two together: since any given states are produced without interrupting the cause-fruit continuity of any given
combination of conditions, the whole expression “dependent origination” (paṭicca-samuppāda) represents the middle way,
vsm2.17:24.2: which rejects the doctrines, “He who acts is he who reaps” and “One acts while another reaps” (S II 20),
vsm2.17:24.3: and which is the proper way described thus, “Not insisting on local language and not overriding normal usage” (M III 234).
vsm2.17:24.4: This, in the first place, is the meaning of the mere words “dependent origination” (paṭicca-samuppāda).
vsm2.17:25.1:
25. Now, in teaching this dependent origination the Blessed One has set forth the text in the way
beginning, “With ignorance as condition there are formations” (S II 20).
vsm2.17:25.2:
Its meaning should be commented on by one who keeps within the circle of the Vibhajjavādins,
who does not misrepresent the teachers, who does not advertise his own standpoint,
vsm2.17:25.3:
who does not quarrel with the standpoint of others, who does not distort suttas, who is in agreement with the Vinaya,
who looks to the principal authorities (mahāpadesa—D II 123ff.),
vsm2.17:25.4:
who illustrates the law (dhamma), who takes up the meaning (attha), repeatedly
reverting to that same meaning, describing it in various different ways.
vsm2.17:25.5: And it is inherently difficult to comment on the dependent origination,
vsm2.17:25.7:
The truth, a being, rebirth-linking,
And the structure of conditions,
Are four things very hard to see
And likewise difficult to teach.
vsm2.17:25.8: Therefore, considering that to comment on the dependent origination is impossible except for those who are expert in the texts:
vsm2.17:25.9:
Whilst I would now begin the comment
On the structure of conditions
I find no footing for support
And seem to founder in a sea.
vsm2.17:25.10:
However, many modes of teaching
Grace the Dispensation here,
And still the former teachers’ way
Is handed down unbrokenly.
vsm2.17:25.11:
Therefore on both of these relying
For my support, I now begin
Its meaning to elucidate:
Listen therefore attentively.
vsm2.17:26.1: 26. For this has been said by the former teachers:
vsm2.17:26.2:
Whoever learns alertly this discourse
Will go from excellence to excellence,
And when perfected, he will then escape
Beyond the vision of the King of Death.
vsm2.17:27.1: 27. So as regards the passages that begin: “With ignorance as condition there are formations” (S II 20), to start with:
vsm2.17:27.2:
(1) As different ways of teaching, (2) meaning,
(3) Character, (4) singlefold and so on,
(5) As to defining of the factors,
The exposition should be known.
vsm2.17:28.1:
28. 1. Herein, as different ways of teaching: the Blessed One’s teaching of the dependent origination
is fourfold, namely, (i) from the beginning; or (ii) from the middle up to the end;
vsm2.17:28.2: and (iii) from the end; or (iv) from the middle down to the beginning. It is like four creeper-gatherers’ ways of seizing a creeper.
vsm2.17:29.1:
29. (i) For just as one of four men gathering creepers sees only the root of the creeper first, and after
cutting it at the root, he pulls it all out and takes it away and uses it,
vsm2.17:29.2:
so the Blessed One teaches the dependent origination from the beginning up to the end thus: “So,
bhikkhus, with ignorance as condition there are formations; … with birth as condition ageing-and-death” (M I 261).
vsm2.17:30.1:
30. (ii) Just as another of the four men sees the middle of the creeper first, and after cutting
it in the middle, he pulls out only the upper part and takes it away and uses it,
vsm2.17:30.2:
so the Blessed One teaches it from the middle up to the end thus: “When he is delighted with, welcomes,
remains committed to that feeling, then delight arises in him.
vsm2.17:30.3: Delight in feelings is clinging. With his clinging as condition there is becoming; with becoming as condition, birth” (M I 266).
vsm2.17:31.1:
31. (iii) Just as another of the four men sees the tip of the creeper first, and seizing the tip,
he follows it down to the root and takes all of it away and uses it,
vsm2.17:31.2:
so the Blessed One teaches it from the end down to the beginning thus: “‘With birth as condition, ageing-and-death,’
so it was said. But is there ageing-and-death with birth as condition, or not, or how is it here?
vsm2.17:31.3: —There is ageing-and-death with birth as condition, so we think, venerable sir.
vsm2.17:31.4:
‘With becoming as condition, birth,’ so it was said … ‘With ignorance as condition there are formations,’
so it was said. But are there formations with ignorance as condition, or not, or how is it here?—There
are formations with ignorance as condition, so we think, venerable sir” (M I 261).
vsm2.17:32.1:
32. (iv) Just as one of the four men sees only the middle of the creeper first, and after cutting
it in the middle and tracing it down as far as the root, he takes it away and uses it,
vsm2.17:32.2:
so the Blessed One teaches it from the middle down to the beginning thus: “And these four nutriments, bhikkhus:
what is their source? What is their origin? From what are they born? By what are they produced?
vsm2.17:32.3: These four nutriments have craving as their source, craving as their origin, they are born from craving, produced by craving.
vsm2.17:32.4:
Craving: what is its source? … Feeling: … Contact: … The sixfold base: … Mentality-materiality:
… Consciousness: … Formations: what is their source? … By what are they produced?
Formations have ignorance as their source … they are … produced by ignorance” (S II 11f.).
vsm2.17:33.1: 33. Why does he teach it thus?
vsm2.17:33.2: Because the dependent origination is wholly beneficial and because he has himself acquired elegance in instructing.
vsm2.17:33.3:
For the dependent origination is entirely beneficial: starting from any one of the four
starting points, it leads only to the penetration of the proper way.
vsm2.17:33.4:
And the Blessed One has acquired elegance in instructing: it is because he has done so through possession of the four
kinds of perfect confidence and the four discriminations and by achieving the fourfold profundity (§304)
vsm2.17:33.5: that he teaches the Dhamma by various methods.
vsm2.17:34.1:
34. But it should be recognized, in particular, that (i) when he sees that people susceptible of teaching
are confused about the analysis of the causes of the process of becoming,
vsm2.17:34.2:
he employs his teaching of it forwards starting from the beginning in order to show
that the process carries on according to its own peculiar laws
vsm2.17:34.3: and for the purpose of showing the order of arising.
vsm2.17:34.4: And (ii) it should be recognized that he employs his teaching of it forwards from the middle up to the end
vsm2.17:34.5: in order to show how the future existence follows on through rebirth from arousing in the present causes for rebirth in the future.
vsm2.17:34.6:
(iii) And it should be recognized that when he surveys the world as fallen upon trouble in the way stated thus,
“This world has fallen upon trouble; it is born, ages, dies, passes away, and reappears” (S II 10),
vsm2.17:34.7:
he employs his teaching of it backwards starting from the end in order to show the laws governing the various
kinds of suffering beginning with ageing and death, which he discovered himself in the early stage of his penetration.
vsm2.17:34.8:
And (iv) it should be recognized that he employs his teaching of it backwards from the middle
down to the beginning in order to show how the succession of cause and fruit extends back into the past existence,
vsm2.17:34.9: and again forwards from the past, in accordance with his definition of nutriment as the source of ignorance (see M I 47f.).
vsm2.17:35.1:
35. Of these methods of presentation, that cited here should be understood to be that stated in forward
order starting from the beginning in order to show to people susceptible of teaching who are confused about
the laws of the process of becoming that the process carries on according to its own peculiar laws,
vsm2.17:35.2: and for the purpose of showing the order of arising.
vsm2.17:36.1: 36. But why is ignorance stated as the beginning here?
vsm2.17:36.2:
How then, is ignorance the causeless root-cause of the world like the Primordial
Essence of those who assert the existence of a Primordial Essence?
vsm2.17:36.4: For a cause of ignorance is stated thus, “With the arising of cankers there is the arising of ignorance” (M I 54).
vsm2.17:36.5: But there is a figurative way in which it can be treated as the root cause. What way is that?
vsm2.17:36.6: When it is made to serve as a starting point in an exposition of the round of becoming.
vsm2.17:37.1: 37. For the Blessed One gives the exposition of the round with one of two things as the starting point: either ignorance,
vsm2.17:37.2:
according as it is said, “No first beginning of ignorance is made known, bhikkhus,
before which there was no ignorance, and after which there came to be ignorance.
vsm2.17:37.3: And while it is said thus, bhikkhus, nevertheless it is made known that ignorance has its specific condition” (A V 113);
vsm2.17:37.5:
according as it is said, “No first beginning of craving for becoming is made known, bhikkhus, before
which there was no craving for becoming, and after which there came to be craving for becoming.
vsm2.17:37.6: And while it is said thus, bhikkhus, nevertheless it is made known that craving for becoming has its specific condition” (A V 116).
vsm2.17:38.1: 38. But why does the Blessed One give the exposition of the round with those two things as starting points?
vsm2.17:38.2: Because they are the outstanding causes of kamma that leads to happy and unhappy destinies.
vsm2.17:39.1: 39. Ignorance is an outstanding cause of kamma that leads to unhappy destinies.
vsm2.17:39.3:
Because, just as when a cow to be slaughtered is in the grip of the torment of burning with fire and belabouring with cudgels,
and being crazed with torment, she drinks the hot water although it gives no satisfaction and does her harm,
vsm2.17:39.4:
so the ordinary man who is in the grip of ignorance performs kamma of the various kinds
beginning with killing living things that leads to unhappy destinies, although it gives no satisfaction
because of the burning of defilements and does him harm because it casts him into an unhappy destiny.
vsm2.17:40.1: 40. But craving for becoming is an outstanding cause of kamma that leads to happy destinies.
vsm2.17:40.3:
Because, just as that same cow, through her craving for cold water, starts drinking cold water,
which gives satisfaction and allays her torment,
vsm2.17:40.4:
so the ordinary man in the grip of craving for becoming performs kamma of the various kinds beginning with abstention from killing
living things that leads to happy destinies and gives satisfaction because it is free from the burning of defilements
and, by bringing him to a happy destiny, allays the torment of suffering experienced in the unhappy destinies.
